steps.title: What are those tiny numbers?
steps.body: Those tiny numbers are called Candidates. They list all of the digits that could possibly be in that cell and we'll use them for our next strategy - Open Singles.

steps.title: Single Candidate
steps.body: In this cell, there is exactly one possible digit (candidate) that can be placed - 5. Let's take a look at why.

steps.title: 3x3 Box
steps.body: The digits 1, 4, 6, and 9 exist within the same box. No duplicates in a box means those values can't possibly be in this cell.

steps.title: Row
steps.body: The digits 7 & 2 also exist within the same row - those values are also left out of that cell's candidates.

steps.title: Column
steps.body: The final digits, 3 & 8 exist within the same column - can't be those digits either!

steps.title: Open Single
steps.body: With candidates displayed, it's easy to see that only the 5 can be in this cell. We call this an Open Single - Give it a tap!

steps.title: Complete the Puzzle
steps.body: The rest of this puzzle can be completed just by finding Open Singles. Hidden Singles won't be available here!

steps.title: P.S. - Multi-selection
steps.body: Tapping multiple empty cells in a row will highlight them all - this is expected! We'll learn more about it later, but for now if you need to clear multiple selections, you can tap a filled cell or tap the cells again! Happy Tapping!
